places.n: Pokémon Café Tokyo, Nihonbashi (ポケモンカフェ 日本橋)
places.ad: Nihonbashi Takashimaya S.C. East Building 5F, Nihonbashi, Chūō City, Tokyo (with Pokémon Center Tokyo DX)
places.w: The world's first Pokémon Café (2018), beside Pokémon Center Tokyo DX; reopened 17 June 2026 after renovation with Pikachu curry, Eevee pancakes, the new Pika Pika Parfait and a live Chef Pikachu show — the Gengar smoothie stays.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Pokémon — the franchise's original themed café, reservation-only, with a live Pikachu show
places.nat: ポケモンカフェ 日本橋

places.n: Rokurinsha, Tokyo Ramen Street (六厘舎 東京ラーメンストリート)
places.ad: Tokyo Ramen Street, Tokyo Station First Avenue B1 (Yaesu side), Marunouchi, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo
places.w: The star of Tokyo Station's eight-shop Tokyo Ramen Street and by far its longest queue — thick tsukemen noodles dipped into a dense pork-and-seafood broth simmered for 13 hours.
places.nat: 六厘舎 東京ラーメンストリート

places.n: Chūkamen-ten Kiraku, Dōgenzaka (中華麺店 喜楽)
places.w: A Dōgenzaka relic serving Tokyo-style noodles since 1952 — shōyu ramen with chewy noodles and crisp fried onions, regulars coming back for decades.

places.n: Tsukemen Gonokami Seisakusho (つけ麺 五ノ神製作所)
places.ad: Sendagaya, Shibuya-ku, Tokyo (by Shinjuku Station south side)
places.w: Queues form an hour before opening for this shrimp-obsessed tsukemen counter, whose creamy shrimp-miso and shrimp-tomato dips are built from hundreds of kilos of otherwise-wasted shrimp shells.
places.nat: つけ麺 五ノ神製作所

places.n: Ramenya Shima, Nishi-Shinjuku (らぁ麺や 嶋)
places.w: Ranked No 1 on Ramen Adventures' best-100 for 2025 and a fixture of Tabelog's Tokyo top three — queues once began at 7am; the rustic shōyu ramen is the bowl to get.

places.n: Chūka Soba Shibata, Komae (中華そば しば田)
places.w: A celebrated chūka-soba champion that relocated to Komae; its duck-and-seafood double soup and punchy soy tare put it at No 4 on Ramen Adventures' 2025 Tokyo best-100.

places.n: Chūka Soba Kamofuku, Hachiōji (中華そば 鴨福)
places.ad: Hachiōji, Tokyo (15 min walk from Hachiōji Station)
places.w: Western Tokyo's most raved-about ramen of 2024 per Time Out and No 5 on Ramen Adventures' 2025 best-100 — worth the trek from Hachiōji Station for its duck-and-Shamo chūka soba.

places.n: Kirby Café Tokyo, Tokyo Solamachi (カービィカフェ)
places.ad: Tokyo Solamachi 4F, Tokyo Skytree Town, Oshiage, Sumida-ku, Tokyo
places.w: Nintendo's pink hero gets his own café on Solamachi's fourth floor under Skytree — Kirby-shaped burgers and pizza, most dishes and drinks served with a collectible, plus an exclusive-goods shop.
places.k: ★ Anime & pop culture — Kirby (Nintendo / HAL Laboratory) — the official character café

places.n: Isetan Shinjuku Depachika (伊勢丹新宿店 食品フロア)
places.ad: Isetan Shinjuku main store B1, 3-14-1 Shinjuku, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
places.w: The flagship Isetan's basement food hall — one of Tokyo's poshest depachika, renovated in 2023, with a fresh market of tasting counters (ham, sausage, oden) and Café Prunier Paris for caviar and champagne.
places.nat: 伊勢丹新宿店 食品フロア

places.n: Ginza Mitsukoshi Depachika (銀座三越 食品フロア)
places.ad: Ginza Mitsukoshi B2–B3, Ginza 4-chōme, Chūō-ku, Tokyo
places.w: Two basement floors under Ginza's landmark department store: B2 for prepared food, Japanese and Western sweets and bakeries; B3 a gourmet supermarket with an outstanding cheese counter and perfect Japanese fruit.
places.nat: 銀座三越 食品フロア

places.n: Asakusa Oden Otafuku (浅草おでん 大多福)
places.w: Founded in 1915 and one of Tokyo's oldest oden houses — paper lanterns, a kept garden and pots of oden simmering in light dashi; a former Michelin Bib Gourmand.
places.nat: 浅草おでん 大多福

places.n: Daikokuya Tempura, Asakusa (大黒家天麩羅)
places.ad: Near Sensō-ji (Denbōin-dōri side), Asakusa, Taitō-ku, Tokyo
places.w: A stone's throw from Sensō-ji, the best known of Asakusa's old tempura houses (alongside San Sada and Owariya), with queues for its tempura and tendon.

The Fukuoka tonkotsu chain famous for customising noodle firmness, richness, garlic and spring onion on a paper form and slurping alone in a partitioned booth — a rite of passage for first-time visitors.
Blue Bottle's first café outside the US (2015), set in a converted warehouse — its arrival made Kiyosumi-Shirakawa Tokyo's specialty-coffee neighbourhood.
A 1930 sweets parlour that escaped wartime damage and still trades from its original wooden building, a designated historic structure — famous for agemanjū and old-school wagashi.
Jimbōchō kissaten opened in 1949 in a narrow alley of the book town, a long-standing literary hangout; credited with introducing Vienna coffee to Japan.
Kissaten in a 1916 Yanaka building, run as a coffee shop from 1938 to 2006 and reopened in 2009 with the original exterior and signage; known for its egg sandwich.

places.n: Arise Coffee Roasters (アライズコーヒーロースターズ)
places.w: Small single-origin roaster in an old corner shop in Kiyosumi-Shirakawa, Tokyo's coffee district; the owner hand-pours each cup and chats with regulars.
places.nat: アライズコーヒーロースターズ

places.w: Tiny Nishi-Shinjuku whisky bar with about 300 bottles, over a hundred of them Japanese incl. sold-out limited editions; the cinephile owner screens silent films while you drink.
Eight-seat counter izakaya a short walk from central Shibuya; the sake sommelier is a hot-sake specialist warming each pour to a precise temperature, paired with a good-value omakase.

places.n: Meikyoku Kissa Lion (名曲喫茶ライオン)
places.w: Tokyo's oldest and best-known classical-music café, first opened in 1926 and rebuilt in 1950; pew-like seats face a 3m Pioneer speaker wall and conversation is discouraged.
Wagashi shop by Gokokuji Station renowned for its large mame-daifuku, mochi wrapped around anko with slightly salty whole beans kneaded in, still sold cheaply.
The shop that started iekei ramen in 1974 — the 家 in 'iekei' honours Yoshimura-ya; its tonkotsu-shoyu soup with spinach and nori spawned Yokohama's whole iekei style.

places.n: Udatsu Sushi, Nakameguro (宇田津 鮨)
places.w: Hisashi Udatsu's art-gallery-like sushi counter hidden in Nakameguro's backstreets — textbook nigiri that sneaks in surprises, with paintings on the walls; listed in the MICHELIN Guide.

places.ad: On the Meguro River, Aobadai, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
places.w: Opened March 2019 as the fifth and then-largest Starbucks Reserve Roastery: a four-floor Kengo Kuma building clad in Japanese cedar beside the Meguro River's cherry trees, roasting on site with coffee cocktails upstairs.

Frying tonkatsu since 1939 with hardly a change: a long counter wraps the open kitchen so diners watch the cooks at work, and the benches round the room are always full of people queuing for a counter seat.

places.ad: 1F, Garden City Shinagawa Gotenyama, 6-7-29 Kitashinagawa, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo 141-0001
places.w: Chef Shuzo Kishida's modern French dining room in Gotenyama — one of Tokyo's eleven three-MICHELIN-star restaurants in the 2026 guide.

places.n: RyuGin, Tokyo Midtown Hibiya (日本料理 龍吟)
places.ad: 7F, Tokyo Midtown Hibiya, 1-1-2 Yūrakuchō, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 100-0006
places.w: Seiji Yamamoto's celebrated Japanese restaurant, moved from Roppongi to the 7th floor of Tokyo Midtown Hibiya — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

places.n: Kioicho Fukudaya (紀尾井町 福田家)
places.w: A traditional ryōtei in Kioichō serving seasonal Japanese cuisine — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
Takahashi Harutaka's Ginza Edomae sushi counter — three MICHELIN stars ('exceptional cuisine') in the 2026 guide.

places.n: Azabu Kadowaki (麻布 かどわき)
places.w: Toshiya Kadowaki's Azabu-Jūban Japanese restaurant — three MICHELIN stars ('exceptional cuisine') in the 2026 guide.
Tomoya Kawada's Minami-Azabu Chinese restaurant in a quiet house — one of Tokyo's eleven three-MICHELIN-star restaurants in the 2026 guide.
Shiseido's historic Ginza French restaurant, opened in 1973 — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

places.n: L'Effervescence, Nishi-Azabu (レフェルヴェソンス)
places.w: Shinobu Namae's Nishi-Azabu restaurant fusing French technique and Japanese produce — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.

places.n: Joël Robuchon, Yebisu Garden Place (ジョエル・ロブション)
places.ad: Yebisu Garden Place, 1-13-1 Mita, Meguro-ku, Tokyo
places.w: The late Joël Robuchon's flagship Tokyo dining room in the faux-château at Yebisu Garden Place (Meguro-ku side) — three MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.
places.nat: ジョエル・ロブション

places.n: Sushi Kanesaka, Ginza (鮨 かねさか)
places.w: Shinji Kanesaka's basement Ginza sushi counter, the mothership of a group with branches abroad — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.
A small Jingūmae restaurant holding two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
Nakameguro restaurant promoted from one to two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
Fine-dining restaurant in the Kabutochō financial quarter — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.

places.ad: 3F, Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioichō, 1-3 Kioichō, Chiyoda-ku, Tokyo 102-0094
places.w: Tasting-menu restaurant on the third floor of Tokyo Garden Terrace Kioichō — two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 guide.
Shintomi restaurant listed with two MICHELIN stars in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
Shinjuku 1-chōme sushi counter newly awarded one MICHELIN star in the 2026 Tokyo guide.
A Bib Gourmand in residential Setagaya whose creative cooking is designed around its affinity with sake — meat dishes are an indispensable part of the menu.
A French Bib Gourmand in Ikejiri, near Ikejiri-Ōhashi — good-value cooking in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide.

places.ad: Shibamata 7-chōme, Katsushika-ku, Tokyo (from Shibamata Station to Taishakuten)
places.w: The 200-metre Edo-era approach to Shibamata Taishakuten, lined with wooden shops selling the town's speciality kusa-dango and restaurants serving river fish such as eel and carp — the setting of the Tora-san films.

places.n: Sugoi Niboshi Ramen Nagi, Golden Gai (すごい煮干ラーメン凪)
places.ad: 2F, Shinjuku Golden Gai (G2 Street), 1-1-10 Kabukichō, Shinjuku-ku, Tokyo
places.w: Up a steep stair in an old wooden Golden Gai house, the Nagi chain's 2008 return to its birthplace serves pungent niboshi ramen from sardines boiled for 12 hours — open 24 hours.
places.nat: すごい煮干ラーメン凪

places.n: Togoshi Ginza Shōtengai (戸越銀座商店街)
places.ad: Togoshi, Shinagawa-ku, Tokyo (around Togoshi-ginza Station, Tōkyū Ikegami line)
places.w: Tokyo's longest open-air shopping street — 1.3 km and some 400 shops — where more than 20 shops fry croquettes for snacking on the walk, between yakitori, yakisoba and dango stands.

places.n: Chanko Tomoegata, Ryōgoku (ちゃんこ巴潟)
places.w: Sumo town's favourite chanko-nabe house for nearly 50 years — the wrestlers' hot pot served as lunch sets that change by weekday (pork miso on Tuesdays, duck dumplings on Wednesdays) and by season.

One of Ueno's most popular ramen counters: only Japanese duck and leek, simmered for two days into a clear, sweet, ungamey stock with house-made noodles — the anchor of the Okachimachi 'ramen yokochō' cluster.

places.n: Yanaka Ginza Shōtengai (谷中銀座商店街)
places.ad: Yanaka 3-chōme, Taitō-ku, Tokyo (between Nippori and Sendagi stations, below the Yūyake Dandan steps)
places.w: A 60-shop old-Tokyo shopping street between Nippori and Sendagi, best grazed: beef menchi katsu from Niku no Suzuki (since 1980), cat-shaped taiyaki, manjū and matcha, all below the 'sunset steps'.
Kokubunji's ramen standout, run by alumni of Nagi and Gamushara: the signature 'wahaha' niboshi chūka soba alongside a chicken 'gahaha' and an 'ahaha' tsukemen.

places.n: Tsukemen Enji, Kichijōji (つけ麺 えん寺)
places.w: A hugely popular Kichijōji tsukemen shop and a food-magazine favourite, known for the bamboo mat in the noodle bowl that drains stray broth.

places.n: Ozawa Shuzo — Sawanoi Sake Brewery, Ōme (小澤酒造 澤乃井)
places.ad: Sawai, Ōme, Tokyo (a few steps from JR Sawai Station, on the Tama River)
places.w: Tokyo's oldest brewery, founded 1702 in the Okutama hills: free tours of kura buildings over 300 years old, then a tunnel to the riverside Sawanoi-en garden to taste ten sakes by the cup — plus a sake shop and tofu restaurants.

A sake brewery since 1863 (Tamajiman) that revived beer-making in 1998 after a 111-year pause — tour 19th-century kura and the Zougura museum, then drink Tama no Megumi or Tokyo Blues at the on-site Italian beer hall.

Founded in the last years of the 19th century and rebuilt after the 1923 earthquake in the two-storey timber house it still occupies: one dish only, chicken sukiyaki bubbling in a cast-iron pot over glowing charcoal.

places.n: Curry Bondy, Jimbōchō (欧風カレー ボンディ)
places.w: The Jimbōchō shop credited with creating 'European-style' curry — a roux built on veal stock and demi-glace simmered over days; up a flight above a bookshop, queues at lunch, and first winner of the Kanda Curry Grand Prix (2011).
places.nat: 欧風カレー ボンディ

places.n: Daily Chico, Nakano Broadway (デイリーチコ)
places.ad: B1F, Nakano Broadway, Nakano, Nakano-ku, Tokyo
places.w: A basement stand in Nakano Broadway famous for its towering eight-layer soft serve in rotating flavours — a snack stop amid the otaku shops.

places.n: Teuchisobadokoro Shisen-an (手打蕎麦処 紫仙庵)
places.w: A Michelin Bib Gourmand hand-made soba shop tucked into a residential street some distance from Meguro Station.
places.nat: 手打蕎麦処 紫仙庵
